name: Budapest Gambit
summary: Against the queen-pawn opening, Black gives a pawn for fast piece play, then wins it back with active knights and a bishop check.

goal.title: Give a pawn for quick piece play, then win it back
goal.text: Black lets White keep an extra pawn at first. In return Black's pieces jump out fast: a knight attacks the extra pawn from the edge of the board, the other knight joins it, and a bishop comes out with check. Within a few moves Black wins the pawn back and enjoys the more active pieces.
plans: Attack the extra white pawn with a knight from the edge of the board, and bring the other knight to help.
Give a check with the dark-squared bishop to drag White's pieces onto awkward squares.
Put the queen next to the king to add pressure on the same pawn.
Take the pawn back as soon as it is safe, then castle.

variations.name: 4.Bf4: Rubinstein variation
variations.strategy: You have won the pawn back and Black's pieces are the more active: both knights are in the center and White's knight is pinned against the king. The middlegame plan is to castle, bring a rook to the center file, and keep the pin going so White cannot complete development comfortably. If you trade your bishop for the pinned knight, White gets the bishop pair, so only do it when it costs White time or structure, and keep the position closed afterwards.

versus.text: The gambit push is right after 2.c4: White's d-pawn must take and your pieces get active at once. Against the quiet 2.Bf4 or 2.Nf3 you take space with the d-pawn instead.

variations.name: 4.Nf3: Adler variation
variations.strategy: Material is level and Black has no weaknesses, but White has a bigger pawn center, so the middlegame is about whether that center is strong or just a target. Develop, castle, and undermine it with pawn breaks like the d-pawn and c-pawn pushes. If White kicks the knight with a pawn, retreat it to a good square instead of letting it be trapped. Black's pieces are well placed and White's space can become a liability.

variations.name: 7.a3? Ngxe5!: the Budapest trap
variations.strategy: This line is about a tactic rather than a long plan. White grabs the offered bishop, and the knight jumps next to the king with check. Its departure lets your queen pin White's e-pawn, so the pawn cannot capture the knight, and White's own pieces block every escape square. If White never falls for it, the normal Budapest plans apply: active knights, a healthy center and quick development.

variations.name: 3.e3: White declines the gambit
variations.strategy: White has declined the gambit, so there is no pawn to win back. The middlegame has a classic structure: White ends up with an isolated central pawn. Your plan is to trade pieces, since fewer pieces mean fewer attacking chances for White, and to place a knight directly in front of the isolated pawn as a blockade. Then target that pawn with your other pieces and look for a favorable endgame.

variations.name: 3.Nc3: White develops instead of taking
variations.strategy: White has more space but is behind in development, so use that. Pressure the center pawn along the open file with a rook, keep pressure on the knight, and prepare a central pawn break while White's king is still in the middle. Black's pieces come out with tempo and the position stays level, so aim for activity and pressure rather than a quick trade.

variations.name: 3.d5: White closes the center
variations.strategy: The center is closed, so the fight moves to the wings. White has more space and is comfortably better here, so do not wait: place your knights well, perhaps with one heading to an outpost, and prepare a break, either a side pawn push to challenge White's space, or a king-side pawn break to gain room and prepare play against White's king once it castles. Keep your pieces flexible and do not hurry the break before it is prepared.

variations.name: 2.Bf4: no gambit, take the center
variations.strategy: White's active bishop is the main target. Offer to trade it with your own bishop so that White's recapture opens a file and pulls a pawn off the center. Pressure the center with a pawn and a knight, castle, and use the queen on the side to pressure the queen-side. Black can open the center with a pawn break once the pieces are developed.

variations.name: 2.Nf3: no gambit, take the center
variations.strategy: Black has taken space and developed with tempo. After the queen comes out, the pawn advance on the queen side gains more space and locks that wing, so White's natural break is a push in the center. Black's plan is to keep the queens on, or trade them for an open file on the side, develop the remaining pieces calmly, and use the extra space on the queen side for a later pawn break. The position is level, so play for a healthy structure rather than hurrying.
